extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent practitioners needing MPEP guidance)
extracted.subtask_short: prior art evaluation for patent examination
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for identifying, obtaining, and determining the prior-art effect of patent and non-patent documents during U.S. patent examination, including domestic and foreign publications, application publications, abandoned files, patent families, and relevant search resources. Covers procedural steps (ordering files, translations), legal dates (filing, publication, patenting, earliest effective filing date), and available search services and databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canceled matter in U.S. patent files
rubrics_metrics.description: Canceled matter in the application file of a U.S. patent or U.S. application publication is not a proper reference as of the filing date under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e); however, matter canceled from the file wrapper may be used as prior art as of the patent or publication date (i.e., as prior public knowledge or prior public availability under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite cases such as Ex parte Stalego and In re Lund. See also related MPEP sections (§ 2127, § 2136.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering of patented and abandoned application files
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural requirements for examiners to inspect previously abandoned or patented file wrappers (paper files or Image File Wrapper (IFW)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IFW files can be viewed via the Patent Examiner’s Toolkit; paper files are ordered via File Ordering System (FOS) requiring art unit, employee number, and patent/application numbers. FOS returns status (accepted, remote warehouse, not located, previous request unfilled, invalid number). Files Repository personnel deliver and return files to requesters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandoned applications as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: A published abandoned application is available as prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a) and 102(b) and 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as of its patent application publication date; a published abandoned application may also be available under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as of the earliest effective U.S. filing date and under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as of its effective filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 37 CFR 1.11(a) the specification, drawings, and papers of an abandoned published application are open to inspection and copies may be obtained; matter available to public under 37 CFR 1.14 may be prior art as of its public availability date. Case law: In re Heritage, In re Lund, In re Switzer, Ex parte Peterson, Ex parte Clifford. Also see MPEP § 2127, § 2136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpublished abandoned application availability
rubrics_metrics.description: File contents of unpublished abandoned applications may be made available to the public where identified or claimed in patents, statutory invention registrations, U.S. patent application publications, or international publications (PCT Article 21(2)). Subject matter available under 37 CFR 1.14 may be used as prior art as of the date it became publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should check 37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(iv) and MPEP guidance on availability and effective dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending applications confidentiality and limited exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending U.S. applications that have not been published are generally confidential (37 CFR 1.14(a)), but claims in one nonprovisional application may be rejected on claimed subject matter of a copending nonprovisional application of the same inventive entity; special rules apply for common assignee/applicant situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 804 and § 2127 (subsection IV) for copending application practices and for exceptions allowing use of copending filings as references.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIPA publication rules and exceptions (publication/nonpublication of applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the AIPA (1999) most patent applications filed on/after Nov 29, 2000 are published 18 months after earliest filing date unless certain exceptions apply or applicant requests nonpublication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications will not be published if: (A) no longer pending, (B) subject to secrecy order (35 U.S.C. 181), (C) provisional application, (D) design patent application (35 U.S.C. 171), (E) international design application (35 U.S.C. 382), (F) reissue application (35 U.S.C. 251). Also see 37 CFR 1.215, 1.219, 1.221 and MPEP § 1122 for nonpublication request procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art effect of U.S. patent application publications
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. patent application publications are prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a) and 102(b) and 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as of the publication date; under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e)(1) and 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) an application publication is prior art as of the earliest effective U.S. filing date of the published application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. application publications of National Stage or WIPO publications under PCT Article 21(2) may be prior art as of the international filing date only with certain conditions (filed on/after Nov 29, 2000, designated U.S., published in English). See MPEP § 2128 and § 901.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. patents: prior art dates and series
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of patenting (on face) is the publication date usually cited; the filing date is ordinarily the effective date as a reference. A pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) date of a U.S. patent can be an earlier effective U.S. filing date; 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) prior art date of a U.S. patent issued from a nonprovisional application claiming benefit of a prior domestic or foreign filing may be the filing date of the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 2127 II, 2136, 2154.01(b). The section also describes historical patent series (X-series, 1836 series, Reissue, A.I., Plant, Design) and citation conventions (e.g., Re. prefix, D. for design).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificates after issuance and their prior art effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-issuance certificates (reexamination certificates, certificates of correction, post-grant review certificates, inter partes review certificates, derivation certificates) amend patents and have specified prior art/legal effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination certificate changes are incorporated into the patent and the prior art date for subject matter in the certificate is same as prior art date for the reexamined patent (35 U.S.C. 307, pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 316). Certificates of correction are part of the original patent (35 U.S.C. 254, 255). PGR/IPR certificates cancel or confirm claims and incorporate new/amended claims as appropriate; derivation certificates may correct inventorship or cancel claims after PTAB decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: INID codes (identification of bibliographic data)
rubrics_metrics.description: INID (Internationally agreed Numbers for the Identification of (bibliographic) Data) codes are used to identify data appearing on the first page of patent documents without language knowledge and have been used on U.S. patents since August 4, 1970.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all codes apply to every country; USPTO recommends identifying documents by: country code (US), patent/publication number, and WIPO ST.16 kind code (e.g., 'US 7,654,321 B1' or 'US 2003/1234567 A1'). See MPEP § 901.05(b) for list of INID codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kind codes (WIPO ST.16) for patent documents
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO ST.16 'kind codes' (letters and sometimes numbers) distinguish kinds and levels of patent documents (application publication, patent, reexamination certificate, reissue, plant, design, AIA-trial certificates, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables list legacy and current kind codes (A1/A2/A9 for application publications; B1/B2 for patents; C1... for reexam certificates; E for reissue; H for SIR; P1/P2/P3/P4/P9 for plant; S for design; J/K/O for PGR/IPR/Derivation certificates). USPTO recommends including country code, number, and kind code when citing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign patent documents — availability as references
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign patents, published applications, and other published derivative material that have been disseminated to the public are available to U.S. examiners as references; however, a foreign patent or its contents should not be cited until its date of patenting or public availability (e.g., publication date) can be confirmed by examiner review of a copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider delays between grant and publication in some countries. Consult MPEP § 901.05(a) for country-specific information and STIC for retrieval assistance. See MPEP § 707.05(e) for data used in citing foreign references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variations in foreign patent practices affecting prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign patent systems differ from U.S. practice with respect to events (grant, publication, public availability), applicants vs inventors, what 'application' means, publication of pending applications (laying open vs printed), administrative systems (examining vs nonexamining), oppositions, and patents of addition — all of which affect when a foreign document becomes prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should analyze country-specific practices: e.g., some countries 'lay open' applications (sufficient to be printed publication under pre-AIA 102), some publish specifications at ~18 months, opposition publications may serve as printed publications, and patents of addition should be identified and cited appropriately. See MPEP § 901.05 I.A–I.G and paragraph V for country details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of contents of pending (foreign) applications as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a foreign law publishes the contents of pending applications (either by laying open for public inspection or by printed publication, commonly ~18 months after filing), those publications constitute printed publications and are available as prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)/102(b) and 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as of the date of publication or laying open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a 'laying open' only posts notice but allows inspection/ordering copies, that suffices for 'publication' under U.S. law (see In re Wyer). Determine the exact date (publication or lay-open) for prior-art effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative systems and scope of foreign searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign patent offices vary in the extent of substantive examination and scope of prior-art searches (some are nonexamining/registration countries; others examine on merits and search domestic and/or foreign material).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand whether a foreign office performs substantive search results or only formalities, as this impacts the weight and content of foreign search reports and the availability of references. Some countries require disclosure of corresponding application references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition proceedings as a source of prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: In countries with opposition systems, a published notice for opposition or printed publication of the application can constitute prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)/102(b) and 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider timing of publication for opposition and whether the document was available to the public during opposition period; opposition filings may raise grounds equivalent to invalidity and may be relevant for prior-art determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corresponding specifications in a family of patents and priority/priority dates
rubrics_metrics.description: A family of patents (same invention filed in multiple countries) may yield corresponding specifications; priority rights under the Paris Convention mean related filings can establish earlier effective dates for patent documents in the family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a U.S. patent claims benefit of earlier foreign or domestic filings, the prior-art date of the U.S. patent may be that earlier filing date (see MPEP § 2154.01(b), § 2136 et seq.). Examiners should trace priority chains across family members to determine earliest effective dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpatent publications and STIC services
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonpatent literature (NPL) — scientific and technical publications, abstracts, defensive publications, borrowed publications, Alien Property Custodian publications — can be prior art if they were disseminated to the public; the Scientific and Technical Information Center (STIC) assists examiners in locating NPL and obtaining copies, dates, and translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STIC offers EIC support, interlibrary loans, chemical and sequence searching, foreign patent services, patent family searches, translations, on-site photocopying, and can obtain earliest publication/distribution dates. Examiners may request legal/litigation searches, patent family searches, and translations via STIC forms or contact staff. See MPEP § 901.06(a) and related paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alien Property Custodian (A.P.C.) publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications vested in the Alien Property Custodian during WWII were published in 1943 as A.P.C. published applications; these are printed publications effective from their publication date and should be cited as 'A.P.C. Application of..., Ser. No..., Published ...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not refer to A.P.C. publications as patents. The Patent Search Room maintains a complete set of these publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstracts, Abbreviatures, and Defensive Publications as references
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts and Abbreviatures are USPTO publications of abandoned applications; Defensive Publications are USPTO publications of provisionally abandoned applications. These publications are references and have assigned document numbers (statutory invention registrations replaced defensive publications after 1985).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defensive Publications and Statutory Invention Registrations are included in subclass lists and subscription orders. Note numbering conventions and conversion tables for older Defensive Publications. See MPEP § 901.06(d) and § 711.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent family information and databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent family information (corresponding patents and publications) is available primarily via commercial databases (e.g., Derwent WPI, INPADOC) and via Office tools (Common Citation Document, Examiner’s Toolkit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WPI in-house is preferred for abstracts, inventor/name searches, IPC searches, and publication dates; INPADOC for quick publication date/family queries. Examiners can request patent family searches via STIC or use automated search tools; public can order foreign patent copies from Foreign Patents Service Center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global Dossier Public Access for related application file histories
rubrics_metrics.description: Global Dossier Public Access provides online access to file histories of related applications from participating IP offices, including PCT and WIPO-CASE participating offices. It shows Office Actions (with machine translations), citations, classification data, Office Action Indicators, Collections view, and download ability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Global Dossier to view file histories, machine translations, and to identify applications with office actions; see WIPO-CASE for participating offices and additional info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations and use of Translations Service Center
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may consult translators in the Translations Service Center for oral help translating foreign language patents and documents; written translations of pertinent portions or full translations can be requested; a database of prior translations is maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written translations can be requested for documents cited or considered for citation. Translations are indexed by country and patent number; copies of outside translations should be furnished to the Translations Service Center for filing. See MPEP § 901.05(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining and confirming publication dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for the earliest date of publication or first distribution to the public of publications should be made to STIC EIC; for U.S. publications, STIC can obtain the day and month claimed by the copyright owner; for foreign publications, similar correspondence can establish dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishing the correct publication or distribution date is critical for prior-art impact. Use STIC services to document exact dates when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online searching tools and special searches (sequences, chemical structures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may conduct online searches for nucleic/amino acid sequences using in-house systems or commercial databases; training and assistance are available from STIC and vendors. Commercial databases can be used after SPE approval and vendor training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence searching is conducted by STIC EIC staff using in-house systems; introductory classes and individual assistance are available. For chemical structures and DNA sequences, STIC/EIC staff can help; examiners can obtain commercial database access upon SPE approval and vendor training via USPTO Learning Center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlibrary loans and borrowed publications for NPL retrieval
rubrics_metrics.description: STIC will obtain journal articles or book chapters not available in-house via interlibrary loan for official business purposes upon request from examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests can be submitted to STIC EIC or via electronic form on STIC NPL website. See MPEP § 901.06(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation data and use of foreign patent citation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should use citation data (bibliographic and other significant data) when citing foreign references and consult provided country-specific guidance and STIC for accurate citation and availability confirmation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 901.05(a)–(c) and § 707.05(e) for the types of citation data and procedures for obtaining copies and confirming dates before citing. Use Official Gazette(s), concordances, indexes, and Foreign Patents Service Center assistance as needed.
